subject: Pilot extension: FocusTech short trial — credits vs invoice offset
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@focustech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@focustech.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — short trial extension and runbook for surge

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for hosting the short evaluation environment last week — the team made good progress. We’re hitting one intermittent throughput limit in our end-to-end tests and would like to ask for a ~3 week extension to the mini-pilot so we can validate the fix and run the additional scenarios.

Two constraints from our side: finance prefers not to add another invoice this quarter, and procurement needs clear language on what happens to unused capacity if we don’t convert.

Options we discussed internally:
- Add 3 weeks to the timebox (no additional invoice) — but that would require you to reserve capacity and there’s some risk on your side for un-utilized hours.
- Issue a small invoice for a credit bucket that we can consume during the extension (finance-friendly, shows commitment).

Can you outline what Redwood would be comfortable with? If you can send the minimal amendment language and a usage snapshot, that helps us move quickly.

Appreciate it — Sam
VP Product, FocusTech

--
Attachment: pilot_usage_report.csv (CSV summary, 2 pages)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@focustech.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@focustech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short trial extension and runbook for surge

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the usage snapshot. Quick thought: we can do either path but each has operational tradeoffs. Two concrete proposals below so procurement/finance have options to review: 

1) Timebox extension (3 weeks) — No upfront invoice. We reserve the capacity and monitor usage. If utilization stays below the agreed threshold (<30% of reserved burst), Redwood will invoice a one-time buffer fee equal to 10% of the reserved burst estimate. This protects our scheduling and is the leanest path for your finance team.

2) Credit bucket — FocusTech prepays a small credit (suggest $7,500) applied to any consumption during the extra 3 weeks. Unused credit rolls into a refundable credit that can be applied to a first paid contract within 90 days, or we can return unused balance as an invoice credit. This gives finance a clean spend line and avoids capacity reservation risk for us.

I’ve looped in Lauren from Finance and Dev from Solutions so we can describe exact invoice/escrow flows. I’ll attach a short amendment draft you can review; it’s intentionally minimal.

Proposed next steps:
- Sam / Priya: pick preferred option (1 or 2) by EOD tomorrow
- Lauren: if option 2, confirm invoice timing and refundable-credit language
- Dev: confirm there’s no infra-side blocker on our end for 3 weeks of reservation

Attaching the draft amendment now.

Thanks,
Ava
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-pilot-amendment-draft.docx (Word doc, 1 page)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@focustech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short trial extension and runbook for surge

Hi all — quick finance note so procurement has clarity. If FocusTech picks option 2 (credit bucket):

- We’ll generate an invoice for the credit ($7,500) with net-30 by default.
- Unused credit: refunded via invoice credit if no paid contract within 90 days; if refund is requested prior to any conversion, we can process within 15 business days after the end of the extension.
- Escrow alternative: if procurement insists on escrowed funds, we can support placing the credit in a third-party escrow (we’ve done this before) but that incurs a one-time admin fee of $250 to cover escrow processing.

Operationally for option 1 (timebox only) — we require a short clause stating Redwood can reallocate reserved capacity if utilization is below 10% for a continuous 7-day period; that prevents us having idle dedicated bursts. The 10% reallocation threshold is negotiable up to 30% as Ava noted.

Let me know which path you prefer and I’ll ask billing to prep the invoice or LaurenBilling to stand by for escrow instructions.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@focustech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@focustech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short trial extension and runbook for surge

Ava / Lauren — thanks for the fast turnaround. After syncing with finance and procurement, FocusTech prefers option 2 (credit bucket) because it gives us an auditable spend line this quarter. A few clarifications we need in the amendment/draft before signing: 

- Please reflect the refundable credit language (refund if no conversion in 90 days).
- Add an SLA statement for the reserved capacity during the 3-week extension (target response time for incidents, and a remedy if we see repeated throttling).
- If escrow is a simple path (and only $250 fee), we’d prefer escrow so the payment sits in a neutral place — please confirm the escrow agent you’ve used previously.

If you can revise the amendment with the above bullets and send a DocuSign link, we’ll get this signed within 24 hours. Appreciate the quick help here.

Sam
VP Product, FocusTech
